previewDocument.text: A type scale is a set of decisions, not a set of sizes
Choosing a ratio is the easy part. The work is deciding what each size is for, and holding that line as a product grows.

Body text is the size most people spend the most time with, so it should be chosen first and everything else derived from it. Picking a display size first tends to produce scales that look impressive in a specimen and read badly in a paragraph.
If two sizes are close enough that nobody can tell them apart, they are not two sizes.
A step that has no purpose will be used for something eventually, and usually for the wrong thing. Fewer, well-named sizes are easier to hold to than a long ramp of near-identical values.

previewLanding.text: Finish the piece in one place
Blueprint is a studio for colour, type and layout. Build the tokens, then preview them on a page the way a client will.
No card needed to try it
Three things Blueprint keeps in one workspace.
Colour, type and spacing live as one set of tokens, so a button in preview matches the export.
Headings, captions and body keep their roles when the page leaves the studio.
Sign-off happens on a real page. No screenshot thread.
Blueprint stores the type decisions with the palette. A heading stays a heading when it leaves the studio, so design is not a second transcription.
When something is stuck, you talk to someone who uses Blueprint. They have seen the same tokens you have.
Not a pile of extras. The few things that keep a page together.
One set of roles for every surface, so a caption looks like a caption everywhere.
The chrome stays out of the way while you read.
See the page as a client will, while you are still editing.
Open the same preview on a phone and keep the tokens.
We stopped guessing hex in three files. The tokens came with the page, which was the whole point.
Plans that stay out of the way
Start with a product. Add people when the system needs them.
Try Blueprint on a page you already have
Open a workspace, paint the tokens, and see whether the type holds.
